alignments.note: Rule 66: high priest, where priest glosses the base lexeme.
Participle rendered finite; the preverb ἀνα- gives up inside the verb's own unit (rule 106).
Rule 32's contrast: a prepositional phrase has no verb to carry the relativizer, so the article keeps they … that, headed on the pronoun.
Rule 53: the prepositional predicate carries the supplied copula.

Corrected: ἡ οὖσα αἵρεσις is article + attributive participle + expressed head noun, so rule 31's test — whether the article governs an expressed head noun — puts the supplied relativizer on the participle, which is the verb that carries it. The unit is headed on is, the word realizing εἰμί. The chapter writes the identical construction at 5:22 (οἱ … παραγενόμενοι ὑπηρέται → the officers that came), analysed the same way (rule 24).

Corrected: rules 31 and 57 — an article in attributive position governs its head noun across the interposed participle and is that noun's own determiner, so it takes the English the. Reading ἡ as substantival and giving it which under rule 32 is the competing analysis, but rule 31 confines that to an article governing no expressed head noun.
Corrected: the head noun stands bare, its determiner having gone to the article that governs it; the noun is arthrous, so rule 51's supplied-determiner clause does not reach it (rule 57).
Rule 21: of + the on the article.
Rule 88: the juncture introducing the finite verb is its helper; subject and auxiliary ride along, headed on filled.
Rule 21's determinerless clause: with stays with the noun.

review_notes: Corrected ἡ οὖσα αἵρεσις: the accepted alignment treated ἡ as substantival (which), οὖσα as a bare is, and αἵρεσις as anarthrous with a supplied the. The article stands in attributive position before the participle and its expressed head noun, which is rule 31's own test for telling an attributive article from a substantival one, and rule 57 forbids deciding the question from the interposed word.

The chapter's parallel at 5:22 — οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι ὑπηρέται → the officers that came — already reads the same shape with the on the article and the relativizer on the participle, so the correction makes the chapter consistent under rule 24.
οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ untouched: they … that on the article under rule 32's prepositional-phrase contrast, were with on σύν under rule 53.
